referents.why: Masculine singular object of the weqatal 'you will say to him' in cl2. The command in cl1 sends Moses to Pharaoh, so the one spoken to is Pharaoh, not Moses.
referents.category: pronoun object of a command to speak

referents.why: First person 'my' inside the speech introduced by the thus-says clause cl3. The speaker of that speech is the LORD (w14), so 'my people' is the LORD's people.
referents.category: first person inside a quoted speech

referents.why: First person 'me' in the purpose clause cl5, still inside the LORD's quoted speech. The speaker is the LORD (w14), not Moses, who is the nearer person in the wider narrative.
referents.category: first person inside a quoted speech

referents.why: Second masculine singular implied subject of the imperative 'go' in the speech the LORD addresses to Moses (cl0 frame). The addressee is Moses (w4).
referents.category: implied you of a command to the addressee

referents.why: Second masculine singular of the weqatal 'you will say', continuing the command to Moses in the same person. The addressee of the outer speech is Moses.
referents.category: implied you of a command to the addressee

referents.why: Second masculine singular imperative 'let go' sits inside the LORD's speech that Moses is to deliver. The one told to let the people go is Pharaoh, the addressee of that inner speech (w7).
referents.category: implied you inside a commanded speech

referents.why: Third masculine plural yiqtol 'that they may serve me' refers to the people (w17), the group let go. The noun is singular in form but is a collective taking a plural verb.

links.why: Self-link from the parser; a clause cannot follow itself. The narrative continuation from the previous verse is an across-verse link, outside this verse's links.
The weqatal in the same person after the imperative continues the same line of commanded action. The fused waw gives 'and then' with no change of person.
Waw joins a command to a yiqtol in a different person, and the link type says this is 'so that', not a plain 'and'. Replaced by the purpose link below.
links.category: command joined to a change of person

links.why: The people are to be let go in order that they may serve the LORD. Waw plus a third-person yiqtol after a second-person imperative is a purpose.
The LORD's words to Moses are the command collection imp1 (go, and say), taken as a whole, not only its first command.
links.category: speech introduced by a narrative clause

links.why: Moses is told to say something, and what he says opens with the thus-says clause cl3, the frame of the LORD's speech.
The thus-says clause introduces the LORD's words, which are the command group imp4 (let go, so that they serve), taken whole.

groups.why: The LORD's speech to Moses. Its parts are the command group imp1 and the commanded turn g1 that Moses is to deliver. The builder listed the bare clauses cl1 and cl2 instead of the group.
groups.category: speech containing a command and a commanded speech

groups.why: Two second-person commands joined by waw at one level: go to Pharaoh, and say to him. The builder gave cl2 the role part, which the imperative kind does not have. The weqatal is a further command, not a result, since it is not third person.
groups.category: commands joined by and at one level

groups.why: The commanded turn: Moses saying to Pharaoh what the LORD has told him to say. Its frame is the saying clause cl2, which also sits in imp1 as a command, and its part is the LORD's speech turn1, nested inside it as the speech-nest rule requires.
groups.category: commanded speech nested in a speech

groups.why: The LORD's words to Pharaoh, framed by the thus-says clause cl3. The builder had the command clauses cl4 and cl5 as bare parts and no addressee. The addressee is Pharaoh (w7), and the commanded collection is the group imp4.
One command, let the people go, and its aim, that they may serve. The aim role is the purpose the command is for. The builder gave cl5 the role part.
